headline: PBOC trims outright repo rollover, lifting 2Y; 10Y CCDC grinds to new low of 1.604% as stocks cool
summary: CGBs bull-flattened in a quiet session. The CCDC 10-year slipped 0.4bp to 1.604%, another 1-year low, while the 30-year was flat at about 2.042% and the 1–3Y rose about 0.5bp after the PBOC rolled over less 3-month outright repo funding, flattening 2s10s 1bp to 38.2bp. Policy banks beat CGBs at the front end, with CDB 2-year down 1.4bp and ADBC and EXIM 3-year down 2–3bp, but lagged at 10Y: CDB 10-year rose 0.2bp to 1.648%, widening to 4.4bp over CGB, and ADBC 10-year was flat at 1.682%.
drivers: PBOC leans against the funding slide

The PBOC rolled over only RMB300bn of 3-month outright reverse repos against RMB500bn maturing, a RMB200bn net drain after a RMB200bn net add in October. Analysts read it as a signal not to treat the switch to the 1.25% overnight anchor as a rate cut after DR001 fell to about 1.259% on Wednesday; the 1–2Y CGBs rose about 0.5bp and TS futures slipped 0.03%.

The PBOC ran RMB263bn of overnight reverse repos at 1.25% against RMB372.5bn maturing, a RMB109.5bn net drain, yet overnight Shibor eased to 1.263% and 14-day to 1.339%, the lowest since May; 1-year AAA NCD yields hit a record low near 1.39% on Wednesday. That fed the policy bank front end, where ADBC 3-year fell 2.6bp and EXIM 3-year 2.3bp.

The Shanghai Composite rose just 0.1% and ChiNext gave back most of a 3% gain, so the equity drag on bonds eased after Wednesday's surge; turnover was about RMB2.12tn. US 10-year Treasuries fell about 7bp and Brent dropped about 10% below $100 after Democrats won Congress, helping T and TL futures settle 0.05% and 0.08% higher.

ADBC sold 1, 3, 5 and 10-year taps at 1.3097%, 1.3661%, 1.4451% and 1.6732%, the 5-year and 10-year below CCDC valuations of 1.461% and 1.682%. Inner Mongolia's local bonds drew cover of about 19–25 times at 1.63% for 10 years and 2.12% for 20 years, showing deep demand for duration; Huafa-linked credits stayed volatile without hitting rates.
data: Oct RatingDog services PMI (Nov 4)
50.8 (f 51.5, p 51.6); composite 52.0 (p 52.4); selling prices cut for a 2nd month
Slowest services growth since July with falling prices supports low yields, though bonds sold off later on equities.
Oct RatingDog mfg PMI (Nov 2)
52.0 (f 51.6, p 52.1); output fastest since April; 11th month of expansion
Private and export-facing firms are holding up, which tempers the weak official print but did not stop the bond rally.
Oct official PMIs (Oct 31)
Mfg 49.3 (f 50.0, p 50.1); new orders 49.4; non-mfg 49.7 (p 50.2); composite 49.7
Back in contraction with softer prices, which supports low yields and the case for continued easy funding.
Q3 PBOC loan report (Oct 28)
Property loans RMB50.08tn, −5.2% y/y; mortgages RMB35.91tn, −4.1% y/y (−1.1tn YTD)
Households keep paying down mortgages, so credit demand stays weak and banks keep buying bonds.
Sep industrial profits (Oct 27)
A beat driven by AI hardware, metals and oil-linked prices, not households; bonds looked through it.
Oct MLF (Oct 26)
RMB700bn 1Y vs RMB900bn maturing (net −200bn); outright reverse repos +400bn net in Oct
A tidy-up, not tightening: medium-term liquidity is still up RMB200bn in October, and the overnight rate is now the policy signal.
Q3 GDP (Oct 19)
Firmer growth, near the bottom of the 4.5–5% target. It eases pressure for stimulus but was not strong enough to sell bonds.
view: Neutral leaning long for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.58–1.64% CCDC range. Funding is anchored at 1.25% overnight, the PBOC is still buying CGBs, oil and global yields are falling and data are soft, so the drift stays lower; but the smaller outright repo rollover shows the PBOC will resist a further fall in funding rates, which caps the front end and limits how far the curve can rally from here. I would buy the 10-year only on a back-up to 1.635–1.64%, keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch, stay underweight policy banks against CGBs at 10Y and the long end, and prefer ADBC/EXIM over CDB. A renewed equity surge or a credit or redemption scare would push the 10-year back to 1.65%, while weak October trade, inflation or credit data could take it through 1.60%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year rose 0.6bp to 1.221%, still near its 1-year low (about the 1st percentile, average 1.308%), and the 1-year 0.5bp to 1.171%, after the PBOC trimmed its 3-month outright repo rollover. The central bank is signalling it will not let funding fall far below the 1.25% anchor, so there is little room left at the front end.
buckets.call: Hold; add 2-year CGBs only above 1.27%, or if the overnight rate is cut below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: 2s5s10s fell 0.6bp to −17.8bp, near the 1-year rich extreme (about the 3rd percentile, average −7.7bp), and 5s7s10s is −9.5bp (0th percentile). The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp is at 28.0bp (about the 65th percentile, average 26.5bp), 1bp in the money and inside the 31bp stop, as the 10-year again outperformed the 5-year.
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The re-buy level of 1.635–1.64% was not reached; the 10-year fell 0.4bp to 1.604%, a fresh 1-year low and 7.8bp lower over the month. Against neighbours it still screens cheap: 7s10s20s is −24.2bp, in about the 83rd percentile against a −29.4bp average, so it remains the preferred point for duration.
buckets.call: Wait; buy 10-year CGBs at 1.635–1.64%, target 1.60%, stop 1.665%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: The 30-year was flat at about 2.042%, near its 1-year low, and 10s30s steepened 0.5bp to 43.9bp, about the 31st percentile against a 45.6bp average. 30s50s at 12.4bp (8th percentile) leaves the ultra-long block little cushion ahead of Nov–Dec supply, even with strong demand for long local bonds.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.05%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: CDB 10-year widened 0.6bp to 4.4bp over CGB, about the 6th percentile against a 9.8bp average; the switch from ~3bp is open and 1.4bp in the money. The front end went the other way: CDB 2-year tightened 2bp to 11.6bp, a 1-year low, as cheap funding pulled in carry buyers, so the trade stays at 10Y.
buckets.call: Keep the CDB 10Y into CGB 10Y switch from ~3bp, target 8bp, stop 1bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 3.4bp more than CDB (about the 77th percentile, average 1.3bp) and EXIM 2.4bp (63rd percentile, average 2.0bp), each about 0.2–0.3bp tighter as CDB lagged. ADBC's 10-year tap cleared at 1.6732%, below the 1.682% curve, so the pickup reflects supply and liquidity rather than credit.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC/EXIM 10Y rather than CDB 10Y for the ~3bp pickup.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: CDB 20-year is 4.9bp over CGB, at its 1-year low (1st percentile, average 10.6bp), and the 30-year 11.0bp, also a 1-year low (average 12.7bp). Policy bank long bonds again moved one for one with CGBs, leaving no spread cushion if supply picks up into year-end.
buckets.call: Prefer CGB 20–30Y to CDB 20–30Y; revisit policy bank long bonds above a 13bp 30-year spread.

watch: Next: US payrolls (Nov 6), October FX reserves (Nov 7) and trade data (expected around Nov 7–10), October CPI/PPI and credit data next week, daily PBOC overnight operations at 1.25%, front-loaded November local bond supply, the FX RRR hike taking effect on Nov 15, October activity data in mid-November and the LPR on Nov 20.
